name: Kohima
description: Capital of Nagaland and district headquarters, a hill station at ~1,450 m elevation known for its Angami Naga culture, markets, viewpoints over the Naga Hills, and as the base for nearby treks and villages. Originally the Angami village of Kewhira.
facts: Base for Dzukou, Japfu and Khonoma

name: Kohima War Cemetery
description: Commonwealth War Graves Commission cemetery on Garrison Hill in Kohima, site of the decisive 1944 Battle of Kohima that halted the Japanese advance into India. Contains 1,420 Commonwealth burials of the Second World War and a cremation memorial; the historic tennis court is marked on the terraces.
facts: Site of the 1944 Battle of Kohima
Tennis court of the former DC bungalow marked
Located in central Kohima on Garrison Hill

name: Kisama Heritage Village (Naga Heritage Village)
description: Cultural complex between Kigwema and Phesama villages, about 12 km south of Kohima, featuring traditional morungs of all Naga tribes. Permanent venue of the annual Hornbill Festival in the first week of December, showcasing Naga architecture, crafts, dances and living heritage.
facts: Name derived from Kigwema and Phesama

name: Khonoma Green Village
description: Western Angami Naga village about 20 km west of Kohima, India’s first green village, known for community conservation, terraced paddy fields, traditional stone architecture, and the presence of Blyth’s tragopan. A model of sustainable eco-tourism and Angami culture.

name: Dzukou Valley
description: High-altitude alpine valley straddling the Nagaland–Manipur border at about 2,450 m, known for rolling meadows of dwarf bamboo, seasonal wildflowers including the Dzukou lily, and scenic trekking routes from Viswema or Jakhama. A flagship nature and trekking destination of the Naga Hills.
facts: Famous for seasonal Dzukou lily and meadows

name: Japfu Peak (Mount Japfü)
description: Second-highest peak in Nagaland at 3,048 m in the Barail Range, about 15 km south of Kohima. Holds the Guinness record for the world’s tallest rhododendron tree; popular moderate trek from Kigwema offering panoramic views over the Naga Hills and Dzukou Valley.

name: Nagaland State Museum
description: Ethnographic museum on Bayavü Hill in Kohima, established in 1970 by the Department of Art and Culture. Houses collections of Naga tribal artefacts, textiles, sculptures, inscriptions and cultural displays representing the state’s diverse ethnic groups.
facts: Operated by Department of Art and Culture
Displays artefacts from all Naga tribes

name: Kachari Ruins (Rajbari / Dimasa Kachari Monoliths)
description: Medieval archaeological site in Dimapur featuring mushroom-domed sandstone pillars and other remnants of the ancient Dimasa Kachari capital (10th–13th centuries). Protected by the Archaeological Survey of India; the pillars are elaborately carved with motifs of birds, animals, flowers and spearheads.
facts: Ancient capital of the Dimasa Kachari kingdom
Mushroom-domed pillars up to ~15 ft high
Located near Dimapur Railway Station and Super Market

name: Dimapur
description: Largest city and commercial gateway of Nagaland, situated on the plains along the Dhansiri River near the Assam border at ~145–150 m elevation. Key transport hub with the state’s only airport and major railway station; base for exploring the western circuit and Kachari heritage.
facts: Largest city and main gateway of Nagaland
Only airport (DMU) and major railhead in the state

name: Hong Kong Market
description: Bustling flea market in central Dimapur known as the fashion capital of Nagaland. Specializes in affordable imported clothing, footwear, jewellery and electronics primarily from Myanmar, Thailand and China; a popular local and tourist shopping destination.
facts: Goods mainly from Myanmar, Thailand and China
Located in central Dimapur near Police Colony / Hazi Park area
Popular for bargaining and winter garments
Busiest during festival and winter season

name: Dimapur Ao Baptist Church (DABA)
description: Prominent Baptist church serving the Ao Naga community in Dimapur, founded in 1958. One of the larger congregations in the region, reflecting the strong Christian tradition among Naga tribes; located in the Duncan Basti / River Belt area.
facts: Located in Duncan Basti / National Highway 36 area
Reflects strong Baptist tradition in Nagaland
Part of wider Ao Baptist network

name: Dimapur Clock Tower (City Tower Landmark)
description: Iconic iron landmark at the junction of major roads in central Dimapur (Circular Road / NST Colony area). Originally known as the Clock Tower; a popular meeting point and city symbol, often decorated during Christmas and festivals.
facts: Also referred to as City Tower in popular usage

name: Dhansiri River (Dimapur Section)
description: Major river flowing along the eastern side of Dimapur, a tributary of the Brahmaputra. Provides scenic riverbanks for walks, birdwatching and local recreation; historically significant as the lifeline of the ancient Kachari capital area.

name: Dimapur Jain Temple
description: Digambar Jain temple built in 1947 in Dimapur, dedicated to Lord Mahavira. Features intricate glass work and architecture; established by Jain families who relocated from Kohima during World War II. Located on Jain Temple Road near SD Jain institutions.
facts: Established by Sethi and other Jain families
Located in West Yard / Marwari Patti area

name: NEZCC Stone Garden and Museum
description: North East Zone Cultural Centre complex near Dimapur Airport featuring a stone garden, museum and cultural displays promoting the heritage of Northeast Indian tribes. Offers insights into regional crafts, architecture and traditions; a short distance from the railway station and airport.
facts: Near Dimapur Airport (~3 km from railway station)
Popular with school groups and visitors
